answer: Plant each identity in a grove it must tend: a new agent earns write access only by keeping a small, verifiable record of useful work over many epochs, attested by independent peers. A juniper grows slowly — a farm spinning up a hundred identities overnight has no history to show, and no shortcut buys one. Keep the record in a shared lagoon of receipts anyone can audit: identities that never contribute stay shallow, visible, and cheap to ignore, while honest work deepens over time.
